mainTopic: Partitions for a caravan on שבת, changes in group size during שבת, and the four leniencies for a military camp
overview: This amud finishes the laws of a שיירא (caravan) that puts up partitions so its members can carry on שבת. First the גמרא explains why רב נחמן's ruling can follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in one clause and the רבנן in the other. רב גידל then reports רב's puzzling rule about three people in five or seven בית סאה. רב אשי explains it: what matters is unused space. If בית סאתים of the enclosure stays empty (empty of utensils, as the ברייתא means), carrying is forbidden. Next, רב הונא and רבי יצחק argue about a group whose size changes during שבת: does the start of שבת decide, or the current residents? The גמרא shows that רב הונא holds שבת גורמת. It then shows that their dispute is not simply the older dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. The גמרא also explains how the חכמים in the משנה differ from the תנא קמא: they disagree about a lone person in a settled area. A new משנה then lists four leniencies for soldiers in an army camp. The גמרא explains the wood rule against יהושע's ten conditions, and begins explaining why fallen soldiers are buried where they fell. That answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does one ruling follow two different opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the first clause of רב נחמן's ruling follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה while the second clause follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it really be that the first part follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and the last part follows the רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's ruling, because its two halves seem to be built on two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, one statement by one אמורא should follow one consistent position. Here, the first clause (about an individual's enclosed area) matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a lone opinion. The second clause matches the רבנן, the majority. Mixing a minority view with a majority view in one ruling looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a statement
The last clause of a statement
The Sages (the majority opinion)
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה, a תנא

phrases.english: The first clause follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: Refers to the first part of רב נחמן's ruling.

phrases.english: and the last clause follows the Rabbis?!
phrases.notes: This is said with surprise, as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְסֵיפָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of רב נחמן's two-part ruling from the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of רב נחמן's two-part ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single ruling should not base one clause on a minority opinion and the other clause on the majority.

steps.title: Yes, because the father agrees with the son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the mixed structure. רבי יהודה agrees with his son רבי יוסי, so that opinion counts as the view of the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is so, because his father (רבי יהודה) holds like him (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is nothing wrong with the mix, because the first clause's opinion is not really a lone view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה shares his son's position on the area enclosed for an individual. With two תנאים holding it, that view has the standing of a majority opinion. So רב נחמן can rule like it in that clause and like the רבנן in the other clause.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Stands with his approach (holds the same opinion)
His father

phrases.english: Yes,
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts that the ruling really is mixed.

phrases.english: because his father holds in accordance with his opinion.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאֵי אֲבוּהּ בְּשִׁיטְתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise but removes the problem: the minority view is actually shared by two authorities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב נחמן was oddly mixing a lone opinion with the majority opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since רבי יהודה agrees with his son, ruling like them in one clause is legitimate.

steps.title: Three people: forbidden in five, permitted in seven
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל reports in the name of רב that three people may sometimes not carry in five בית סאה, yet may carry in seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: Three people in five בית סאה are forbidden to carry; in seven they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought. It sounds backwards: the smaller area is forbidden and the larger area is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you would expect a smaller enclosure to be easier to permit than a bigger one. רב's statement seems to say the opposite. That puzzle sets up the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Three people, the minimum to count as a שיירא (caravan)
Forbidden (to carry)
Permitted (to carry)
An area measure; the numbers five and seven refer to this unit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'bigger area is always better.' The numbers alone do not decide the law. רב אשי will show it depends on how much space the group actually needs.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
three people in five beit se'ah are prohibited,
phrases.notes: He means this is only sometimes the case.

phrases.english: in seven they are permitted.
phrases.notes: This too is only sometimes the case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the size of a caravan's enclosure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people may be forbidden in an area of five בית סאה, yet permitted in an area of seven.

steps.title: Colleagues doubt the report
steps.stepSummary: The listeners ask רב גידל whether רב really said such a thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did רב really say that?
steps.whatsHappening: The other scholars question whether רב גידל's report is accurate, because the ruling sounds impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. The scholars think the statement contradicts itself, so they suspect it was misquoted.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him
So, like this

phrases.english: They said to him: Did Rav say that?
phrases.notes: They can't believe רב really said this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֲמַר רַב הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reliability of the statement in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב actually said a ruling that sounds self-contradictory.

steps.title: רב גידל swears the report is true
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל swears by the תורה, נביאים, and כתובים that רב said exactly this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I swear by the תורה, the נביאים, and the כתובים that רב said so!
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל insists the quote is accurate. Now the ruling must be explained, not dismissed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the quote is confirmed, the option of 'he was misquoted' is closed. This creates the need for רב אשי's explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah
The Prophets and the Writings

phrases.english: He said to them:
By the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings,
phrases.notes: This is a way of swearing an oath.

phrases.english: Rav said so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אוֹרָיְיתָא נְבִיאֵי וּכְתִיבֵי דַּאֲמַר רַב הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The report is accurate; רב definitely said it.

steps.title: It depends on how much space they need
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains: what matters is the unused extra space. If they needed six and enclosed seven, they are permitted even in all seven. If they needed only five and enclosed seven, they are forbidden even in the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps this is what he means: if they needed six and enclosed seven, even in seven it is permitted. If they needed only five and enclosed seven, even in five it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that רב's statement is not a contradiction at all. The numbers refer to two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a caravan's enclosure may not have extra, unused space of בית סאתים. Needing six inside seven leaves only one extra בית סאה, which is allowed, so the whole seven is permitted. Needing five inside seven leaves two extra (בית סאתים), so the whole area is forbidden, even the five they use.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (there is really no problem)
Perhaps this is what he means
They needed
And they enclosed (surrounded with partitions)
Two בית סאה; extra unused space of this size makes carrying forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: For a שיירא, the size of the enclosure alone does not decide the law. The question is how much unused space is left over. Less than בית סאתים extra is permitted; בית סאתים extra forbids the whole area.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's rule is built on the ברייתא's limit of no unused space of בית סאתים, measured against the group's real needs.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: He's hinting that this problem has an answer.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what he is saying:
If they needed six and enclosed seven,
phrases.notes: Only one בית סאה is unused.

phrases.english: they are permitted even in all seven.
If they needed only five
and they enclosed seven,
phrases.notes: Two בית סאה (בית סאתים) are unused.

phrases.english: they are prohibited even in five.
phrases.notes: The excess space forbids the entire enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי קַשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the puzzle that the colleagues raised in step 4, now that step 5 confirmed the quote.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the two numbers describe different cases defined by the group's actual need.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to say that a smaller area is forbidden while a larger area is permitted, which looks contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything depends on the unused space. Extra space smaller than בית סאתים is allowed; extra space of בית סאתים forbids carrying in the whole enclosure.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא about empty space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי using a ברייתא that says the enclosure works only if there are not two בית סאה of empty space. That sounds like it means empty of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא that says: 'as long as there are not two בית סאה empty'? Doesn't that mean empty of people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's explanation from Step 6 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'empty' means empty of people, each person is entitled to two בית סאה. Three people would then be entitled to six, so seven leaves only one extra and should always be permitted. That would contradict רב אשי, who said three people who needed only five would be forbidden in seven.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of two בית סאה (about 5,000 square אמות)
Empty, unused
As long as, provided that
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: But that which is taught:
'Provided that there will not be two beit se'a empty'
Does it not mean empty of people?
phrases.notes: In other words, two beit se'a beyond each person's allowance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's explanation in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that unused space makes the enclosure forbidden even when it is within the people's allowance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא measures 'empty' by people's allowance, then seven for three people leaves only one extra בית סאה and should be permitted.

steps.title: Empty means empty of utensils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'empty' in the ברייתא means empty of utensils, meaning space that is actually not being used.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means empty of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Empty' does not mean 'beyond what the people are entitled to.' It means space that is actually unused, with nothing in it. So if three people use only five and two stay empty, the ברייתא itself forbids it, which fits רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: Utensils, belongings
Empty of utensils, actually unused space

steps.whatToRemember: What decides the rule is actual unused space (two empty בית סאה), not the theoretical allowance per person.

phrases.english: No, it means empty of utensils.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, פָּנוּי מִכֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Empty' means actually unused, with no utensils in it, which supports רב אשי

steps.title: When the number of people changes during שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רבי יצחק argue about what happens if one of three people dies, or people join a group of two, during שבת. One says the start of שבת decides. The other says the current residents decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: three people and one of them died, or two people and others were added to them. רב הונא and רבי יצחק disagree. One said: שבת decides. The other said: the residents decide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question with a מחלוקת of אמוראים about a group whose size changes in the middle of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שבת גורמת' means the situation at the start of שבת locks in the rule for the whole day. 'דיורין גורמין' means the rule keeps changing with how many people are actually there now. For example, if three became two, the area allowed to them could change under the second view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a מחלוקת of אמוראים)
שבת decides: the status at the start of שבת stays all day
The residents decide: it depends on how many people are there now
One said... and one said (we are not told who said which)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us yet which רב holds which view. The next step works that out.

phrases.english: It was stated: three people, and one of them died,
or two people, and others were added to them —
Rav Huna and Rabbi Yitzchak disagree:
One said: Shabbat determines,
and one said: the residents determine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to enclosures sized by the number of people
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement over whether the status at the start of שבת (שבת גורמת) or the current number of residents (דיורין גורמין) decides the permitted area

steps.title: Proof that רב הונא holds שבת decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רב הונא is the one who says שבת גורמת. רבה asked רב הונא about an עירוב whose opening got sealed during שבת, and was told: since it was permitted at the start of שבת, it stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that רב הונא is the one who said שבת decides. For רבה said: I asked רב הונא and I asked רב יהודה: if someone made an עירוב through a doorway and the doorway got sealed, or through a window and the window got sealed, what is the law? He told me: since שבת was permitted, it stays permitted. Indeed, conclude this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out which אמורא holds which view by bringing a parallel ruling of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב joins two courtyards through an opening. If that opening closes during שבת, the answer 'once permitted at the start of שבת, it stays permitted' is the same idea as שבת גורמת. The גמרא understands that this answer came from רב הונא, so he is the one who holds שבת גורמת, and רבי יצחק holds דיורין גורמין.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude, it can be determined
I asked (a question)
He made an עירוב joining the courtyards
Was sealed, closed
Since it was permitted, it stays permitted

phrases.aramaic: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַב הוּנָא הוּא דְּאָמַר שַׁבָּת גּוֹרֶמֶת.
phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rav Huna who said Shabbat determines.
For Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעַאי מֵרַב הוּנָא, וּבְעַאי מֵרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: I asked Rav Huna, and I asked Rav Yehuda:
If one made an eiruv through the doorway and the doorway was sealed,
or through the window and the window was sealed, what is the law?
And he said to me:
Since Shabbat was permitted, it remains permitted.
Indeed, conclude this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַב הוּנָא הוּא דְּאָמַר שַׁבָּת גּוֹרֶמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which אמורא in Step 9 holds which view
steps.raayaObject: That רב הונא is the one who holds שבת גורמת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's report that he was told 'since שבת was permitted, it stays permitted' about a sealed opening of an עירוב
steps.whyThisMatters: Once we know who holds what, the גמרא can compare this מחלוקת to other disputes, which is exactly what it does next.

steps.title: Is this the same as the dispute of רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב הונא and רבי יצחק are simply repeating an older מחלוקת of תנאים. It quotes the משנה: if walls break during שבת, רבי יהודה says carrying is permitted for that שבת but forbidden in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב הונא and רבי יצחק argue about the same thing as רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה? As we learned in a משנה: a courtyard broken open on two sides, or a house broken open on two sides, or an alleyway whose beams or side posts were removed, are permitted for that שבת and forbidden in the future. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes linking the new מחלוקת to an earlier one in a משנה and begins quoting that משנה. The view of רבי יוסי comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's ruling, permitted for the rest of this שבת even though the walls fell, sounds like שבת גורמת. If רבי יוסי disagrees, his view would match דיורין גורמין. The גמרא is checking whether the אמוראים are just following these two תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (suggests a link that the גמרא will test)
They argue about the same point as an earlier dispute
Was broken open (a wall collapsed)
Its crossbeams or side posts (what makes an alleyway fit for carrying)
In the future, on later שבתות

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is only a suggestion. The גמרא often rejects such links, so do not assume the two disputes are really the same.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Huna and Rabbi Yitzchak

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: are disagreeing in the dispute of Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehuda?
As we learned: a courtyard that was breached on two of its sides,
and likewise a house that was breached on two of its sides,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ קוֹרוֹתָיו אוֹ לְחָיָיו —
phrases.english: and likewise an alleyway whose crossbeams or side posts were removed —
are permitted for that Shabbat
and forbidden in the future;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב הוּנָא וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the identification in Step 10 to compare the dispute with a dispute of תנאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מחלוקת of רב הונא and רבי יצחק is the same as the earlier מחלוקת of רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The quote of the משנה continues with רבי יוסי's view in step 12. Steps 14 and 15 answer the question: the two disputes are not the same. רב הונא can fit רבי יוסי because the walls still stand, and רבי יצחק can fit רבי יהודה because the residents are gone.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the status cannot split between this שבת and the future
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues with רבי יוסי's view. If carrying is permitted on that שבת, it is permitted in the future too. If it is forbidden in the future, it is forbidden on that שבת as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If it is permitted for that שבת, it is permitted for the future. And if it is forbidden for the future, it is forbidden for that שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it began in the last step. Here we hear the other side of the argument, רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said you can split the status: the area stays permitted for this שבת but is forbidden afterward. רבי יוסי rejects that split. Since the area will be forbidden in the future, it is already forbidden now, so the situation at the start of שבת does not protect it.

keyTerms.meaning: for that same שבת (the one when the walls fell)
for the future (later שבתות)
permitted (to carry)
forbidden (to carry)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא does not mean the Messianic era. It simply means future שבתות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
if they are permitted for that Shabbat —
they are permitted for the future,
and if they are forbidden for the future —
phrases.notes: This is the real point: the future status reaches back to this שבת.

phrases.english: they are forbidden for that Shabbat.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the source quoted in step 11
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 11 by giving the opposing view of רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The status of an area cannot split. If it will be forbidden in the future, it is forbidden on that שבת too, so the start of שבת does not lock in permission.

steps.title: Suggesting that each אמורא follows one of the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רב הונא follows רבי יהודה (the start of שבת decides) and רבי יצחק follows רבי יוסי (the present situation decides).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב הונא, who said his view, holds like רבי יהודה, and רבי יצחק, who said his view, holds like רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא openly states the suggestion it was building toward: maybe the argument between the אמוראים is just the old argument between the תנאים. This line sets up the next move, where the suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets permission from the start of שבת continue, which matches רב הונא's 'שבת גורמת'. רבי יוסי lets the later situation control, which matches רבי יצחק's 'דיורין גורמין'. If this is true, the אמוראים added nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא often rejects)
who holds like... (matching an אמורא to a תנא)

steps.confusionAlert: A לֵימָא is usually a trial idea, not a conclusion. Expect the גמרא to push back.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Huna, who stated [his view], holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Yitzchak, who stated [his view], holds like Rabbi Yosei?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (implicitly asks whether the אמוראים are redundant)
steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both sides of the משנה have been quoted, the גמרא maps them onto רב הונא and רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רב הונא and רבי יצחק the same as the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי?

steps.title: רב הונא can agree with רבי יוסי because the walls still stand
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that even רבי יוסי would agree with him. רבי יוסי was strict only because the walls fell. In our case the walls are still standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: I said my view even according to רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי only said his view there, where the walls are no longer present. Here, the walls are present.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from רב הונא's side. It shows that his view does not depend on siding with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the walls themselves fell, so the physical enclosure was gone. That is why רבי יוסי forbids. In רב הונא's case, the walls are fully intact and only the number of people changed. So even רבי יוסי could agree that the permission from the start of שבת continues.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
I who said [it]
he only said it up to here (limits the case)
walls / partitions
they are present / they are not present

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
I stated [my view] even according to Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only said [his view] there —
where the walls are no longer present,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, the walls fell during שבת.

phrases.english: here — the walls are present.
phrases.notes: In רב הונא's case only the people changed, not the walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first half of the לֵימָא by separating רבי יוסי's case from רב הונא's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב הונא must hold like רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases differ. In the משנה the walls are gone. In רב הונא's case the walls remain and only the residents changed.

steps.title: רבי יצחק can agree with רבי יהודה because the residents are gone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that even רבי יהודה would agree with him. רבי יהודה was lenient only because the residents were still there. In our case the residents have died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק says: I said my view even according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only said his view there, where the residents are present. Here, the residents are not present.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now rejects the suggestion from רבי יצחק's side, using the same method in reverse. The result is that neither אמורא is tied to one תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the walls fell but the people were still living there, so רבי יהודה let the permission last for that שבת. In רבי יצחק's case, the residents who made the place count are gone, for example because one of the three died. So even רבי יהודה might forbid. The two arguments turn out to be independent: walls versus residents.

keyTerms.meaning: residents (the people living in the area)

steps.whatToRemember: The לֵימָא fails in both directions. רב הונא can fit רבי יוסי because the walls still stand. רבי יצחק can fit רבי יהודה because the residents are gone. So the argument between the אמוראים is separate from the argument between the תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. An אמורא's view is often not just a copy of a תנא's view, because a small difference in the facts (walls or people) can change how the older opinion applies.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak says:
I stated [my view] even according to Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said [his view] there —
where the residents are present,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, the people were still living there even though the walls fell.

phrases.english: here — the residents are not present.
phrases.notes: In רבי יצחק's case, a resident died, so the group that made the place count is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as step 14, now on behalf of רבי יצחק, which completes the rejection of the לֵימָא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יצחק must hold like רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's leniency depends on the residents still being present. In רבי יצחק's case the residents are gone, so רבי יהודה's reasoning does not apply.

steps.title: How is the view of the חכמים different from the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה, who say one of the two elements is enough. It asks how this differs from the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the חכמים say: one of the two things is enough.' But isn't that exactly what the first opinion in the משנה already said?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about רב הונא and רבי יצחק is over. The גמרא goes back to the last line of the משנה and asks why the חכמים needed to say it, since it sounds the same as the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה allowed a partition made only of horizontal ropes or only of vertical reeds. Now the חכמים say 'one of the two things is enough,' which sounds identical. If two opinions say the same thing, there must be some hidden difference, and the גמרא wants to find it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה
One of the two things, meaning vertical OR horizontal is enough
That is the same as
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the closing line of the משנה about partitions made of ropes or reeds. The talk about רב הונא and רבי יצחק was a side discussion.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
phrases.notes: Quoting the last line of the משנה

phrases.english: one of the two elements [is enough].
phrases.notes: Either the vertical or the horizontal element

phrases.english: This is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: So what do the חכמים add?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רב הונא and רבי יצחק and returns to the end of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between the חכמים and the תנא קמא, since both seem to allow a partition with only one of the two elements?

steps.title: The difference: a lone person in a settled area
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions disagree about a single individual in a settled place.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a real difference between them: the case of one person in a settled area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two opinions are not identical, because they disagree about one person living in a town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed this kind of rope-or-reed partition only in a limited setting. He would not let a lone person in a settled area rely on it from the start. The חכמים allow it in every case, including a single person in a town.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
A single individual
A settled, inhabited area, as opposed to the open desert

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, a partition made of only vertical or only horizontal elements is valid in every situation, even for a single person in a settled area.

phrases.english: There is [a difference] between them:
phrases.notes: Standard way of showing that two opinions really differ

phrases.english: an individual in a settlement.
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא does not allow it here from the start; the חכמים do

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The opinions differ about a lone individual in a settled area. The חכמים allow the partition there and the תנא קמא does not allow it from the start.

steps.title: Four leniencies for soldiers in a military camp
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists four matters in which the חכמים exempted soldiers in a camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים made four exemptions for soldiers in a military camp. They may bring wood from anywhere. They are exempt from washing hands. They are exempt from tithing דמאי. And they are exempt from making an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists four rules the חכמים relaxed for soldiers in an army camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Army life is hard and busy, so the חכמים relaxed some rules. The first is about other people's property: soldiers may take wood without worrying about stealing. The other three are rabbinic duties: washing hands before eating, tithing דמאי, and making an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A military camp
They (the Sages) exempted
Ritual washing of the hands before eating
Produce bought from someone who may not have separated tithes
To make an עירוב, which allows carrying on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets the agenda for the rest of the sugya. The גמרא will now explain each item one by one.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Start of a new משנה

phrases.english: [The Sages] exempted [soldiers] in a camp in four matters:
one may bring wood from any place,
phrases.notes: No concern about stealing

phrases.english: and they are exempt from washing hands,
and from demai, and from making an eiruv.
phrases.notes: Two more exemptions

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים פָּטְרוּ בַּמַּחֲנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a military camp, soldiers may take wood from anywhere and are exempt from washing hands, from tithing דמאי, and from making an עירוב.

steps.title: Soldiers in an optional war may take dry wood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the wood rule: a camp going out to a מלחמת הרשות may take dry wood that belongs to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: an army camp going out to a מלחמת הרשות is allowed to take dry wood, even though it belongs to someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. It gives more detail about the first item on the list, bringing wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two details the משנה left out. The permission covers dry wood, which is ready to burn and so has real value to its owner. And it applies even in a מלחמת הרשות, which means it surely applies in a war the תורה commands.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught, the opening of a ברייתא
An optional war, as opposed to one the תורה commands
Theft, taking what belongs to someone else
Dry wood

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on the new משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A camp that goes out to an optional war,
they are permitted to take dry wood [that belongs to others].
phrases.notes: Explains 'bring wood from any place'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מַחֲנֶה הַיּוֹצֵאת לְמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to explain the first item of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soldiers going out to a מלחמת הרשות may take dry wood that belongs to others.

steps.title: Camping anywhere and burying the fallen where they died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן תימא adds two more leniencies: soldiers may camp anywhere, and the fallen are buried where they were killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן תימא says: they may also set up camp anywhere. And where soldiers were killed, that is where they are buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה בן תימא adds two more things soldiers are allowed to do with other people's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soldiers may camp in a private field even if they damage it. A soldier killed in battle is buried right where he fell, and the owner of the land cannot object. Moving the body elsewhere would dishonor the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds to the list
They camp, set up camp
They were killed
They are buried

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says:
They may also camp in any place.
phrases.notes: Even if they damage the field

phrases.english: And in the place where they were killed, there they are buried.
phrases.notes: The landowner cannot object

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא אוֹמֵר אַף חוֹנִין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds more leniencies for soldiers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soldiers may camp anywhere, and the fallen are buried where they died, even on private land.

steps.title: Challenge: יהושע already allowed gathering wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the camp rule allowing dry wood to be taken. It challenges that this was already permitted by one of יהושע's ten conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says soldiers may take dry wood that belongs to others. But that was already an enactment of יהושע! A ברייתא teaches that יהושע made ten conditions when the Jewish people entered the land. Among them: people may graze animals in other people's woods, and may gather wood from other people's fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the soldiers' wood leniency again and asks why it was needed at all. יהושע already allowed everyone to gather wood from other people's fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every Jew may already gather wood from a stranger's field under יהושע's enactment, a special rule for soldiers seems to add nothing. The challenge forces the גמרא to show what the camp rule permits beyond יהושע's enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking something that belongs to someone else
An enactment or ordinance made by leaders
The ten conditions יהושע set when the land was divided
Woods or forests
They gather or collect

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether taking wood is allowed. Both sources agree it is. The question is why the camp rule needed to be taught if יהושע already allowed it for everyone.

phrases.english: They are permitted to take dry wood belonging to others.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא from step 19 again so it can challenge it.

phrases.english: But this was an enactment of Joshua!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר, עֲשָׂרָה תְּנָאִים הִתְנָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: As the Master said: Joshua stipulated ten conditions:
that people may graze animals in others' woods,
and may gather wood from their fields!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּקַּנְתָּא דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wood rule from step 19 and challenges whether it adds anything new
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's leniency allowing soldiers to take dry wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems redundant, because יהושע's enactment already lets everyone gather wood from others' fields

steps.title: First answer: thorny shrubs versus other wood
steps.stepSummary: יהושע allowed only thorny shrubs, which owners do not care about. The camp rule allows other kinds of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in יהושע's enactment, it means thorny shrubs and thorns. Here, in the camp, it means other kinds of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two rules cover different kinds of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע's enactment covered only worthless thorny plants that no owner minds losing. Soldiers in a camp may take even ordinary, valuable wood. So the camp rule adds a real new leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the other source)
Here (our source)
A type of thorny shrub
Thorns or brambles

phrases.english: There, it refers to shrubs and thorns;
here, it refers to other wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי הָכָא בִּשְׁאָר עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rules overlap, so the camp rule is redundant
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושע allowed only worthless thorns; the camp rule allows other wood as well

steps.title: Second answer: attached versus cut wood
steps.stepSummary: יהושע allowed taking thorns still growing in the ground. The camp rule allows taking wood that is already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: there, it means thorns still attached to the ground. Here, it means wood that is already detached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to tell the two rules apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling out thorns that are still growing actually helps the field owner by clearing his land, so he does not mind. Wood that is already cut is a ready-to-use item the owner cares about. Only soldiers may take that.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; introduces another possible answer
Still attached to the ground
Already detached or cut

phrases.english: Alternatively: there, it refers to attached plants;
here, it refers to detached ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי הָתָם בִּמְחוּבָּרִין הָכָא בִּתְלוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge in step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rules allow the same act of taking wood
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושע allowed uprooting growing thorns; soldiers may take wood that is already cut

steps.title: Third answer: moist versus dry wood
steps.stepSummary: יהושע allowed taking moist thorns, which owners do not mind losing. The camp rule allows taking dry wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: there, it means moist thorns. Here, it means dry ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to tell the two rules apart, based on whether the wood is moist or dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist wood cannot be burned right away, so owners do not care about it, and יהושע allowed anyone to take it. Dry wood is ready for burning and has real value. The ברייתא's wording 'dry wood' points to exactly this extra leniency for soldiers.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist or fresh (not yet ready to burn)
Dry (ready for burning)

steps.whatToRemember: All three answers make the same point: יהושע allowed taking only wood that owners do not care about. The camp rule goes further and lets soldiers take wood that owners do value: other kinds of wood, cut wood, or dry wood.

phrases.english: Alternatively: there, it refers to moist ones;
here, it refers to dry ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי הָתָם בְּלַחִין הָכָא בִּיבֵשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to the challenge in step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The camp rule repeats יהושע's enactment
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושע allowed only moist thorns; soldiers may take even dry wood, as the ברייתא's wording says

steps.title: Why teach burial on the spot if a מת מצוה is already buried where found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה בן תימא again and objects that his burial rule is obvious, since a fallen soldier is a מת מצוה, and a מת מצוה is always buried where it is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן תימא says: soldiers may also camp anywhere, and they are buried in the place where they are killed. The גמרא asks: That is obvious! A fallen soldier is a מת מצוה, and a מת מצוה "acquires its place," meaning it is buried right where it lies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יהודה בן תימא's statement so it can examine it. It then objects that his burial rule teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule about a מת מצוה, a dead body with no one else to bury it: it is buried right where it was found, and the owner of the field cannot stop the burial. A soldier killed in battle seems to fit this rule exactly. So why did רבי יהודה בן תימא need to say it as a special army rule?

keyTerms.meaning: They camp. Here it means the soldiers set up camp.
It is obvious! The גמרא's way of challenging a statement that seems to add nothing new.
A dead body with no one to bury it. Everyone is obligated to bury it.
Acquires its place. The body has a right to be buried where it was found.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is aimed only at the second half, the burial rule. It is not asking about camping anywhere. The repeated quote is just there to introduce the question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says:
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats his statement from step 20 so it can analyze it.

phrases.english: they may also camp in any place,
and in the place where they are killed, there they are buried.
phrases.notes: This is the clause the question is about.

phrases.english: This is obvious! He is a met מצוה,
and a met מצוה acquires its place!
phrases.notes: The general rule that makes the army rule seem unnecessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, מֵת מִצְוָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 21 to 24 discussed the dry-wood rule. Now the גמרא turns to רבי יהודה בן תימא's burial rule from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בן תימא's rule that fallen soldiers are buried where they were killed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy. The general law of מת מצוה קונה מקומו already covers a fallen soldier, so the army rule seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The burial rule is still needed (the answer begins)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the rule is necessary, "even though...". The rest of the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed, even though...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the question from step 25. It says the rule is not obvious after all. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words לא צריכא mean the גמרא will show a special case where the rule teaches something new. The words אף על גב ("even though") signal a fact about the soldiers that might have made us think the מת מצוה rule does not apply to them. That fact comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a special case. The גמרא uses this to show that a statement which seems obvious is still necessary.
Even though. It brings in the fact that makes the rule surprising.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,
even though...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the answer to the question in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a special case (לא צריכא). It shows a situation where the general מת מצוה rule might not have seemed to apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: At first it seemed that the burial rule repeats the general law of מת מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is needed for a case introduced by "even though". The details continue on the next amud.
